author: BBC News
description:
Professor Michal Pędziwiatr, one of two surgeons who treated victims on the street in the aftermath of a mass shooting in Krakow, has spoken to the BBC about his experience. 
 
Two doctors were eating near the city's Main Market Square on Saturday when a gunman began firing at random, killing six and injuring 15. 
 
"We rushed into the area and started our rescue" before the emergency services arrived, Pędziwiatr said. 
 
The pair raced to treat both the attacker and two officers shot while subduing the perpetrator.

description:
US tech giant Nvidia has begun an investigation following claims its CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

Nvidia is one of the world's largest companies making cutting-edge computer chips that power emerging AI technologies. The company said its board had no reason to believe that its secrets or national security had been compromised.

According to the New York Times, US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security. 

Jensen Huang has admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He said he took "full responsibility" for what he did and had fallen short of his responsibilities to Nvidia's employees, board and shareholders.  He said: “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

Today, Laura and Joe are looking at what might be in a new deal between the UK and European Union.

Laura has spoken to the EU's former Brexit negotiator Michel Barnier, who warns that the UK cannot pick and choose which elements of the EU’s single market it wants to adopt.

author: BBC News
description:
Would you let AI walk around your home?

Meta has reportedly built a humanoid robot called Max and, if Mark Zuckerberg gets his way, this could be the next frontier for artificial intelligence. After years of AI living on our screens, Silicon Valley is now racing to give AI a body, one that can see, hear, move through the world and interact with people in real life.

This week on AI Decoded, we explore the growing race to put humanoid robots into our homes and workplaces. Joining us are John Hanke, founder of Niantic and CEO of Niantic Spatial, Ed Zitron, one of the technology industry's most outspoken critics, and technology researcher and author Stephanie Hare.

Together, they unpack the technical challenges, commercial ambitions and ethical questions behind the push to bring AI into the physical world.

author: BBC News
description:
An attack in Krakow’s Main Market Square on Saturday has left six people dead. 
 
Police said a 25-year-old man drove into the square "before beginning to fire at random people from his car". 
 
Poland's Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the suspect is a Polish national.
 
He added that it looks like he held "very radical views" and that everything indicates he was inspired by "far-right ideologies".
 
One of the six people killed in the attack has been identified as a British national.
 
The head of Poland's police force, Marek Boroń, says 16 more people were injured, including two police officers, five foreign nationals and the suspect.
 
Krakow is also holding two days of mourning, with businesses in the city closed today after the attack.
